title: What If Two Nations Nearly Went to War Over a Pig? In 1859 Two Did

scenes.text: What if two great powers almost went to war over a pig? In 1859, they nearly did.
On an island claimed by both America and Britain, an American settler shot a British company's pig in his garden.
He offered ten dollars. Refused. The British threatened arrest, so the US Army landed about sixty soldiers.
By the end of August, 461 Americans with fourteen cannons faced British warships carrying more than two thousand men.
Ordered to land troops, the British admiral refused to involve two great nations in a war over a pig.
Both sides shared the island for twelve years, until arbitrators gave it to America. The only casualty was the pig.

description:
What if two great powers nearly went to war over a pig? On 15 June 1859, on San Juan Island, which both the United States and Britain claimed, an American settler shot a Hudson's Bay Company pig rooting in his garden. His offer of 10 dollars was refused and British authorities threatened to arrest him.
By 31 August, 461 American soldiers with 14 cannons faced British warships; the British admiral would not 'involve two great nations in a war over a squabble about a pig'. The island stayed under joint military occupation for 12 years until arbitration through the German Kaiser awarded it to the United States in 1872.
